name: Large Die Cut Stickers
seoTitle: Large Die Cut Stickers: Big Logos Cut to Shape, Bulk Runs
seoDescription: Large die cut stickers from 12 inches to 24 by 36 inches, cut to your logo or mascot on laminated vinyl for trucks, walls, glass and team gear. Bulk pricing.
tagline: Logos and mascots from 12 inches to 2 by 3 feet, contour cut so nothing but the artwork goes on the surface.
quickAnswer: Large die cut stickers are printed vinyl graphics from about 12 inches up to 24 by 36 inches in one piece, laminated and cut to the outline of the artwork so a logo or mascot goes on with no background around it. They suit truck doors, trailer sides, gym walls, storefront glass and team equipment. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production after proof approval.

sections.h2: A 2 foot logo with nothing around it
sections.html:
At 2 feet across, a square sticker becomes a sign with a border, and a vinyl background that size shows every ripple, bubble and edge from across the lot. Cutting the sticker to the artwork outline removes the background, so a mascot on a truck door or a crest on a gym wall reads as if it were painted on. That is what this page covers: single pieces from about 12 inches up to 24 by 36 inches, printed on thick white vinyl, laminated, then contour cut.

The sibling is our custom large stickers page, which is for blocks: posters that stick, full-bleed panels, floor graphics and wall murals where the rectangle is part of the design. Choose the custom large sticker page when the edge of the sticker is a straight line you want. Choose this page when the edge is the drawing. The jobs that come through most are team and school logos in bulk, fleet door graphics, mascots for tailgates and trailers, storefront glass, and equipment markings that have to be read from 30 feet.

sections.h2: Bulk die cut stickers for teams, fleets and events
sections.html:
Large die cut orders are rarely for one surface. A school orders 200 crest stickers for a season; a fleet orders a logo for every door on 40 trucks; a tournament orders mascots for coolers, tents and the scoreboard. Bulk runs of the same artwork at 12 to 24 inches cost far less per piece than a sign shop charges per decal, because the print and the cut run continuously instead of one at a time.

  • Sports decals for helmets are small; the large runs go on team trailers, bus sides, locker room walls and the rear windows of parent cars
  • Fleet door logos at 18 to 24 inches, with unit numbers supplied as a separate small sticker
  • Storefront glass graphics, mirror printed to go inside the window where weather cannot reach them
  • Gym and studio walls, on removable adhesive so the paint survives a rebrand
  • Trade show booth walls and counters, applied and peeled in the same week
  • Dumpster, bin and equipment logos on powder-coated steel

Mixed sizes of the same art count toward one order, so a 24 inch truck logo and a 12 inch window version can share a run.

sections.h2: Sizes, viewing distance and how each one goes on
sections.html:
A working rule for lettering: 1 inch of letter height for every 10 feet of viewing distance. A logo is more forgiving than text, but the table below is a fair guide to what each size can do and how it has to be applied. sections.h2: Cutting rules that change once the artwork is big
sections.html:
Small die cut stickers forgive thin lines; big ones punish them. A 0.1 inch tail on a 2 inch sticker is nothing. Scale the art to 24 inches and that tail becomes a 1.2 inch sliver of vinyl that catches on a sleeve. We add bridges behind detached letters, thicken strokes under 0.25 inches and fill tight inside corners, and we show every change on the proof in magenta so you can say no to any of them.

Artwork should be vector (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) wherever possible. A 300 dpi raster file at final size works, but a logo pulled from a website will print soft at 18 inches. Single pieces stop at 24 by 36 inches; beyond that we tile into panels with a 0.5 inch overlap and place seams away from faces and text. Gloss laminate suits vehicles and glass. Matte suits walls under overhead lights, where gloss throws glare across the whole graphic.

sections.h2: Putting a large die cut sticker on flat
sections.html:
1. Clean with isopropyl alcohol. Wax and tire-shine residue on a truck door will lift the sticker within a month.
  2. Tape the sticker in place with the backing on, step back 20 feet and check it is level; a tilt of half an inch shows at this size.
  3. Run a strip of masking tape across the top edge as a hinge.
  4. Lift from the bottom, peel the backing down to the hinge and cut it away.
  5. Squeegee from the hinge downward in overlapping strokes, holding the unstuck part away from the surface so it cannot grab early.
  6. Above 24 inches, or on glass, mist the surface with water and a drop of dish soap first, position, squeegee the water out and leave it 48 hours.
  7. Wait 24 hours before washing and 72 hours before a car wash.

A second person holding the free end makes the difference between a clean 24 inch application and a creased one. Pieces that arrive rolled should lie flat for an hour before you start.

Pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker for the smallest pieces; a 12 inch die cut piece in a run of 100 sits well above that, and the per-piece price falls as the quantity climbs, so a quote with size and count gives the real figure. The minimum is 100 per design. Production is 5 to 7 business days after proof approval, delivery 8 to 10 business days by FedEx, free within the United States. Rush is available if you tell us the date.

Pieces up to 18 inches ship flat with a slip sheet between every ten; larger pieces ship rolled, print side out, in a tube. Defective pieces are reprinted at no charge within the 10 day return window. Large die cut is the biggest end of our custom sticker range, which starts at half an inch and uses the same vinyl and laminate throughout.

faqs.q: How big can a single large die cut sticker be?
faqs.a: One piece goes up to 24 by 36 inches. Beyond that we tile the graphic into panels with a 0.5 inch overlap and mark each seam on the proof, keeping seams away from faces and lettering. Most truck door logos are 18 to 24 inches wide; trailer sides and walls are where tiling comes in.

faqs.q: Can I order bulk die cut stickers in several sizes of one logo?
faqs.a: Yes. The 100 piece minimum applies per design, not per size, so a 24 inch version for trailers, an 18 inch for doors and a 12 inch for windows can share one order. Each size is priced on its own dimensions. Send the artwork once and list the sizes and counts on the quote.

faqs.q: Do large die cut stickers for trucks need a laminate?
faqs.a: Yes, and every piece we ship has one. On a vehicle the printed ink faces sun, car-wash brushes, road salt and fuel splash; the laminate takes that wear instead of the print. With gloss laminate expect typically 3 to 5 years on a vertical panel before the colors soften. Matte laminate lasts the same but shows road film sooner.

faqs.q: Can large die cut sports decals go on a team trailer or bus?
faqs.a: Yes. Trailer sides are flat aluminum or fiberglass and take a 24 inch mascot well. Bus sides have rivets and body lines; keep the sticker between them, because vinyl bridged over a rivet lifts within weeks. Clean with alcohol, use the hinge method, and allow 72 hours before the first wash.

faqs.q: Which adhesive should I pick for large die cut stickers on a gym wall?
faqs.a: Removable. A 2 foot logo on permanent adhesive will pull paint when the wall is redone. Removable adhesive on matte vinyl holds for years on smooth, cured paint and peels clean with a little heat. Wait two weeks after painting before applying, and avoid textured or washable paints with additives.

faqs.q: Why did you add bridges to my large die cut sticker on the proof?
faqs.a: Because a detached element, such as a dot over an i or a separate letter, would arrive as its own loose piece and have to be positioned by eye on a 2 foot graphic. A bridge is a narrow strip of clear or background-color vinyl that keeps the pieces in place. It is marked in magenta on the proof, and you can decline it.

faqs.q: Can a large die cut sticker be applied by one person?
faqs.a: Up to about 18 inches, yes, with the hinge method: tape the top edge, peel the backing down and squeegee from the hinge. At 24 inches and above a second person holding the free end prevents the vinyl from grabbing early and creasing. A wet application with soapy water also gives a solo installer time to reposition.

faqs.q: Does the price of bulk die cut stickers drop at 500 or 1,000 pieces?
faqs.a: Yes. Set-up and proofing cost the same for 100 or 1,000, so the per-piece price falls steadily as the count rises, and the drop is largest between 100 and 500. For a fleet or a league season, order the full year in one run rather than in batches. Pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker for the smallest sizes.

faqs.q: Can a large die cut sticker go on the inside of storefront glass?
faqs.a: Yes. We mirror print the artwork on clear vinyl with a white ink layer behind the colors, so it reads correctly from the street and sits where weather, cleaners and vandals cannot reach it. Apply wet; glass shows every trapped bubble, and the soapy water lets you slide the piece level before squeegeeing.

faqs.q: How do large die cut stickers ship without creasing?
faqs.a: Pieces up to 18 inches ship flat in a rigid box with a slip sheet between every ten. Larger pieces are rolled print side out around a core and shipped in a tube. Unroll them and let them lie flat for an hour before applying. If anything arrives creased or damaged, we reprint it at no charge within the 10 day window.

faqs.q: What file do I need for a 24 inch die cut sticker?
faqs.a: A vector file: AI, EPS, SVG or a PDF with text converted to outlines. Vector scales to any size without softening and gives us a clean path for the cutter. A 300 dpi PNG or JPG at the final 24 inch size also works, but a small web logo will print blurry. Our team can redraw a raster logo as vector before the proof.

faqs.q: How long does a bulk large die cut sticker order take?
faqs.a: Production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free digital proof, and FedEx delivery within the United States is free, so plan on 8 to 10 business days in total. Large runs of several hundred pieces fit inside that window. If you have a season opener or a fleet rollout date, ask about rush on the quote.
